summary: Shoshin Kuwayama is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1957–1961), where he later served as Assistant Professor (~1973–1989) and Professor Emeritus at the Institute for Research in the Humanities (~1966).

Shoson Miyamoto was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Otani University, the University of Tokyo, and the University of Oxford, he held professorships at Tokyo, Komazawa, Toyo, and Waseda, and founded the Japanese Association of Indian and Buddhist Studies.
Shou-chien Shih works in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He served as a Professor at National Taiwan University (~1990) and as director of the National Palace Museum (~2004–2006).

Shozen Kumoi (1915–2017) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and under Erich Frauwallner in Vienna. He served as assistant professor and professor emeritus at Otani University and taught at Bukkyo and Kyoto Universities.
Shri Krishna Saksena is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. Attested in 2016, he held positions as Professor at the University of Lucknow and the University of Hawaiʻi.
Shri Krishna Sharma worked in the fields of Indology and linguistics. He founded the Hindu Maha Sabha and DAV College, Suva.

Shridhar Ramakrishna Bhandarkar was an Indology scholar. In 1884, he was Assistant to the Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College, later serving as Professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College and permanent Professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai.

Shridhar Tryambak Pathak was an Indologist. He held posts as Shastri at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1921) and as Sanskrit Teacher at Elphinstone College (attested 1927).

Shrikant S. Bahulkar is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale. He served as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as a professor at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (attested 2000–2007).

Shrinarayan Mishra is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy who studied under Anantalal Thakur. At Banaras Hindu University, he served as Lecturer in Sanskrit (attested 1971), Reader (attested 1985), and Professor Emeritus of Sanskrit (attested 2010).

Shripad Krishna Belvalkar was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Kashinath Bapu Pathak. He was Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1914–1927), Secretary of BORI (~1918–1927), General Secretary of the All-India Oriental Conference, and General Editor of the Mahabharata (1948–1961).

Shrivatsa Goswami is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied philosophy at Banaras Hindu University. He founded Sri Caitanya Prema Samsthana (1972) and held positions at Banaras Hindu University, Vrindaban Research Institute (attested 1994), and Harvard University.

Shu-chen Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She completed a PhD at the University of Virginia (attested 2007) under Jeffrey Hopkins and Karen Christina Lang, and worked there as a teaching assistant in 1996.

Shu-fen Chen is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. She studied at National Tsing Hua University, where she later served as Professor (attested 2010), and completed doctoral studies under Hans Henrich Hock (attested 2000).

Shubhachandra is an Indology scholar who held a professorship at Karnatak University (attested 2001) and was affiliated with the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore (attested 2002).

Shudo Ishii is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Shigeo Kamata. He spent his career at Komazawa University from assistant to full professor (1971–2014) and served as acting head of Matsugaoka Bunko.

Shuhong Chang was a scholar in archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied in China and France. He taught at Zhejiang University and the National Beiping Art School/Academy, and served as director and honorary director of the Dunhuang Academy (1942–1985).
Shuichi Maida was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University and was a student of Haya Akegarasu.

Shuji Takayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He has held appointments at Ryukoku University (attested 2003), Bukkyo University (attested 2003), Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2006), and Musashino University (attested 2006).
Shujiro Shimada was a scholar of Japanology, Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1928–1931) and held a post at Princeton University (~1962–1975).
